# README.md

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/README.md

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://fluidcad.io/img/logo.png" alt="FluidCAD Logo" width="120" />
</p>

<h1 align="center">FluidCAD</h1>

<p align="center"><strong>Write CAD models in JavaScript. See the result in real time.</strong></p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://fluidcad.io/docs/getting-started">Getting Started</a> &middot;
  <a href="https://fluidcad.io/docs/tutorials/">Tutorials</a> &middot;
  <a href="https://fluidcad.io/docs/guides">Guides</a>
</p>

> FluidCAD is under active development. APIs and features may change as the project evolves.
>
> I'm not accepting pull requests just yet -- I'm still finalizing the design and putting together a roadmap. Once I hit **v0.1.0**, I'd love to have contributions from the community. Stay tuned!

## Under the Hood

FluidCAD is built on [OpenCascade](https://dev.opencascade.org/), a full B-Rep (boundary representation) modeling kernel, through the [opencascade.js](https://ocjs.org/) WebAssembly binding. This means precise, production-grade geometry -- exact edges, fillets, and booleans -- not mesh approximations.

A huge thanks to the [opencascade.js](https://ocjs.org/) team for making this possible.

## Features

### Code-Driven 3D Modeling

Design parametric 3D models using JavaScript. Every change in your code is reflected instantly in the 3D viewport.

```js
import { extrude, fillet, sketch } from 'fluidcad/core';
import { circle } from 'fluidcad/core';

sketch("xy", () => {
    circle(50)
})

const e = extrude(50)

fillet(5, e.startEdges())
```

### Traditional CAD Workflow

A modeling workflow that feels familiar to users of mainstream CAD software -- sketches, extrusions, fillets, shells, booleans, and more -- all driven by code.

### Modeling History

Navigate through your modeling history step by step. Review how any model was built and roll back to any point in the feature tree.

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://fluidcad.io/img/history.gif" alt="FluidCAD History" />
</p>

### Interactive Prototyping

Some operations support interactive mouse-driven input directly in the viewport, letting you prototype faster without writing every parameter by hand.

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://fluidcad.io/img/region-extrude.gif" alt="FluidCAD Region Extrude" />
</p>

### Feature Transforms

Re-apply modeling features based on matrix transformations. Move, rotate, or mirror entire feature sequences to build complex geometry from simple building blocks.

```javascript
sketch("xy", () => {
    rect(200, 100).centered()
})

const e1 = extrude(20)

sketch(e1.endFaces(), () => {
    circle([-80, 30], 30)
});

const pin = extrude(10)

const f = chamfer(2, pin.endEdges());

repeat("linear", ["x", "y"], {
    count: [4, 2],
    length: [160, -60]
}, pin, f)

```
<p align="center">
  <img src="https://fluidcad.io/img/repeat.png" alt="FluidCAD Repeat Feature" />
</p>

### Pattern Copying

Duplicate features in linear or circular patterns to quickly populate repetitive geometry.

### Smart Defaults

Most operations just do the right thing without extra arguments. `extrude` picks up the last sketch, `fillet` targets the last selection, and touching shapes are automatically fused -- less boilerplate, more readable code.

### STEP Import / Export

Import and export STEP files with full color support. Bring in existing CAD models or share your designs with any standard CAD tool.

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://fluidcad.io/img/step-import.png" alt="FluidCAD Step Import" />
</p>

### Use Your Favorite Editor

FluidCAD ships official extensions for **VS Code** and **Neovim**, but works with any editor -- just point the CLI at your project.

### LLM / AI Agent Integration (MCP)

FluidCAD ships an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server so AI agents (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, opencode, etc.) can drive a running workspace -- take screenshots, inspect geometry, edit `.fluid.js` files, and look up the API by symbol. See [Set Up the MCP Server](#3-optional-set-up-the-mcp-server) below.

## Getting Started

### 1. Create a New Project

```bash
mkdir my-app && cd my-app
npm init -y
npm install fluidcad
npx fluidcad init
```

This generates `init.js` and `jsconfig.json` to get you started.

### 2. Set Up Your Editor

<details>
<summary><strong>VS Code</strong></summary>

1. Install the **FluidCAD** extension from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=FluidCAD.fluidcad).
2. Open your project folder in VS Code.
3. Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P`) and run **Show FluidCAD Scene**.

The 3D viewport opens in a side panel and updates live as you edit `.fluid.js` files.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Neovim</strong></summary>

Add the plugin with [lazy.nvim](https://github.com/folke/lazy.nvim):

```lua
{
  "Fluid-CAD/FluidCAD",
  config = function()
    require("fluidcad").setup()
  end,
  ft = { "javascript" },
}
```

Open a `.fluid.js` file and the server starts automatically. Run `:FluidCadOpenBrowser` to open the 3D viewport in your browser.

See the full list of commands in the [Neovim plugin README](extension/neovim/README.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Any Other Editor</strong></summary>

From your project directory, run the FluidCAD server directly:

```bash
npx fluidcad serve
```

This starts a local server and opens a 3D viewport in your browser. Edit your `.fluid.js` files in any editor -- the viewport updates on save.

**Options:**

| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `-w, --workspace <path>` | Path to your project | Current directory |
| `-p, --port <port>` | Server port | `3100` |
| `--open` | Open the viewport in your default browser when ready | _off_ |

</details>

### 3. (Optional) Set Up the MCP Server

FluidCAD bundles an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server so LLM agents can drive your workspace -- screenshots, geometry inspection, source edits, API lookup. It's included in the `fluidcad` package; no separate install needed.

Wire it into your MCP client:

<details>
<summary><strong>Claude Code</strong></summary>

Register at user scope so it's available in every project:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user FluidCAD -- npx -y fluidcad mcp
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Claude Desktop / Cursor</strong></summary>

Add to `claude_desktop_config.json` or `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "FluidCAD": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "fluidcad", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>opencode</strong></summary>

Run `opencode mcp add` and answer the prompts, or add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "FluidCAD": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "fluidcad", "mcp"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

Then install the companion skill so agents follow the FluidCAD workflow:

```bash
npx skills add Fluid-CAD/FluidCAD
```

See the [MCP README](mcp/README.md) for the full tool surface, transport details, and local-testing guide.

# Constraints

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/constraints.mdx

sidebar_position: 4
title: "Constraints"
description: "Constraint qualifiers for constraining geometry relationships in 2D sketches."

# Constraints

Constraint qualifiers control the spatial relationship between geometries in 2D sketches.
They are used with tangent geometry functions like `tLine()`, `tCircle()`, and `tArc()`.

```ts
import { outside, enclosed, enclosing, unqualified } from 'fluidcad/constraints';
```

## Functions

### outside()

```ts
outside(sceneObject: SceneObject): QualifiedGeometry
```

Qualifies a geometry as being on the outside of the constraining object.

| `sceneObject` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The geometry to qualify. |

### enclosed()

```ts
enclosed(sceneObject: SceneObject): QualifiedGeometry
```

Qualifies a geometry as being enclosed by the constraining object.

| `sceneObject` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The geometry to qualify. |

### enclosing()

```ts
enclosing(sceneObject: SceneObject): QualifiedGeometry
```

Qualifies a geometry as enclosing the constraining object.

| `sceneObject` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The geometry to qualify. |

### unqualified()

```ts
unqualified(sceneObject: SceneObject): QualifiedGeometry
```

Removes any existing constraint qualification from a geometry.

| `sceneObject` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The geometry to unqualify. |

---

# aLine()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/aLine.mdx

sidebar_position: 12
title: "aLine"
description: "Draws a line at the given angle with the given length. Chain `.centered()` to center the line on the current position."

# aLine()

Draws a line at the given angle with the given length.
Chain `.centered()` to center the line on the current position.

**Returns**: [**`ALine`**](/docs/api/types/aline)

## Signatures

```ts
aLine(angle: NumberParam, length: NumberParam): ALine
```

Draws a line at the given angle with the given length.
Chain `.centered()` to center the line on the current position.

| `angle` | NumberParam | The angle in degrees |
| `length` | NumberParam | The line length |

```ts
aLine(angle: NumberParam, target: SceneObject): ALine
```

Draws a line at the given angle that ends where it intersects the target
geometry. The nearest intersection along the line's direction (in either
sign) is used.

| `angle` | NumberParam | The angle in degrees |
| `target` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The geometry to intersect with |

```ts
aLine(targetPlane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, angle: NumberParam, length: NumberParam): ALine
```

Draws a line at the given angle on a specific plane.

| `targetPlane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to draw on |
| `angle` | NumberParam | The angle in degrees |
| `length` | NumberParam | The line length |

---

# arc()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/arc.mdx

sidebar_position: 2
title: "arc"
description: "Draws an arc to an end point from the current position. Chain `.radius(r)` to set bulge radius, or `.center(point)` to specify the circle center."

# arc()

Draws an arc to an end point from the current position.
Chain `.radius(r)` to set bulge radius, or `.center(point)` to specify the circle center.

**Returns**: [**`ArcPoints`**](/docs/api/types/arc-points) \| [**`ArcAngles`**](/docs/api/types/arc-angles)

## Signatures

```ts
arc(endPoint: Point2DLike): ArcPoints
```

Draws an arc to an end point from the current position.
Chain `.radius(r)` to set bulge radius, or `.center(point)` to specify the circle center.

| `endPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end point of the arc |

```ts
arc(startPoint: Point2DLike, endPoint: Point2DLike): ArcPoints
```

Draws an arc from a start point to an end point.
By default, uses the current position as the arc center.
Chain `.radius(r)` to use bulge radius instead, or `.center(point)` to specify an explicit center.

| `startPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The start point of the arc |
| `endPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end point of the arc |

```ts
arc(radius: NumberParam, startAngle?: NumberParam, endAngle?: NumberParam): ArcAngles
```

Draws an arc by radius and angle range at the current position.
Angles are measured relative to the current tangent (the tangent of the previous
geometry, or +X when there is none).
Chain `.centered()` to center the arc symmetrically around the start angle.

| `radius` | NumberParam | The arc radius |
| `startAngle` | NumberParam | The start angle in degrees, relative to the current tangent (defaults to 0) *(optional)* |
| `endAngle` | NumberParam | The end angle in degrees, relative to the current tangent (defaults to 180) *(optional)* |

```ts
arc(targetPlane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, endPoint: Point2DLike): ArcPoints
```

Draws an arc to an end point on a specific plane.

| `targetPlane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to draw on |
| `endPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end point of the arc |

```ts
arc(targetPlane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, startPoint: Point2DLike, endPoint: Point2DLike): ArcPoints
```

Draws an arc between two points on a specific plane.

| `targetPlane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to draw on |
| `startPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The start point of the arc |
| `endPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end point of the arc |

```ts
arc(targetPlane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, radius: NumberParam, startAngle: NumberParam, endAngle: NumberParam): ArcAngles
```

Draws an arc by radius and angle range on a specific plane.

| `targetPlane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to draw on |
| `radius` | NumberParam | The arc radius |
| `startAngle` | NumberParam | The start angle in degrees |
| `endAngle` | NumberParam | The end angle in degrees |

---

# bezier()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/bezier.mdx

sidebar_position: 8
title: "bezier"
description: "Draws a bezier curve through the given points. The first argument is the explicit start, the last is the endpoint, and any in between are control points. Sets the sketch cursor to the endpoint. With 0 args: interactive mode placeholder (no geometry). With 1 arg: places only the start point (no curve yet). With 2 args: degree 1 (straight line from start to end). With 3 args: degree 2 (quadratic bezier with 1 control point). With 4 args: degree 3 (cubic bezier with 2 control points)."

# bezier()

Draws a bezier curve through the given points. The first argument is the
explicit start, the last is the endpoint, and any in between are control
points. Sets the sketch cursor to the endpoint.
With 0 args: interactive mode placeholder (no geometry).
With 1 arg: places only the start point (no curve yet).
With 2 args: degree 1 (straight line from start to end).
With 3 args: degree 2 (quadratic bezier with 1 control point).
With 4 args: degree 3 (cubic bezier with 2 control points).

**Returns**: [**`Geometry`**](/docs/api/types/geometry)

## Signatures

```ts
bezier(...points: Point2DLike[]): Geometry
```

Draws a bezier curve through the given points. The first argument is the
explicit start, the last is the endpoint, and any in between are control
points. Sets the sketch cursor to the endpoint.
With 0 args: interactive mode placeholder (no geometry).
With 1 arg: places only the start point (no curve yet).
With 2 args: degree 1 (straight line from start to end).
With 3 args: degree 2 (quadratic bezier with 1 control point).
With 4 args: degree 3 (cubic bezier with 2 control points).

| `...points` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike)[] | Start, optional control points, and end point *(optional)* |

# circle()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/circle.mdx

sidebar_position: 3
title: "circle"
description: "Draws a circle at a given center with an optional diameter."

# circle()

Draws a circle at a given center with an optional diameter.

**Returns**: [**`ExtrudableGeometry`**](/docs/api/types/extrudable-geometry)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/sketching/primitive-shapes) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
circle(center: Point2DLike, diameter?: NumberParam): ExtrudableGeometry
```

Draws a circle at a given center with an optional diameter.

| `center` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The center point |
| `diameter` | NumberParam | The circle diameter (defaults to 40) *(optional)* |

```ts
circle(diameter?: NumberParam): ExtrudableGeometry
```

Draws a circle at the origin with an optional diameter.

| `diameter` | NumberParam | The circle diameter (defaults to 40) *(optional)* |

```ts
circle(targetPlane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, diameter: NumberParam): ExtrudableGeometry
```

Draws a circle with a given diameter on a specific plane.

| `targetPlane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to draw on |
| `diameter` | NumberParam | The circle diameter |

# copy()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/copy.mdx

sidebar_position: 29
title: "copy"
description: "[2D] Creates linear copies along an axis inside a sketch."

# copy()

[2D] Creates linear copies along an axis inside a sketch.

**Returns**: [**`SceneObject`**](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/copying) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
copy(type: "linear", axis: AxisLike, options: LinearCopyOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

[2D] Creates linear copies along an axis inside a sketch.

| `type` | "linear" | Must be `'linear'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The axis to copy along |
| `options` | LinearCopyOptions | Copy count, spacing, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to copy (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
copy(type: "linear", axis: AxisLike[], options: LinearCopyOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

[2D] Creates linear copies along multiple axes inside a sketch.

| `type` | "linear" | Must be `'linear'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like)[] | The axes to copy along |
| `options` | LinearCopyOptions | Copy count, spacing, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to copy (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
copy(type: "linear", axis: AxisLike, options: LinearCopyOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

[3D] Creates linear copies along an axis.

| `type` | "linear" | Must be `'linear'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The axis to copy along |
| `options` | LinearCopyOptions | Copy count, spacing, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to copy (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
copy(type: "linear", axis: AxisLike[], options: LinearCopyOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

[3D] Creates linear copies along multiple axes.

| `type` | "linear" | Must be `'linear'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like)[] | The axes to copy along |
| `options` | LinearCopyOptions | Copy count, spacing, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to copy (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
copy(type: "circular", center: Point2DLike, options: CircularCopyOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

[2D] Creates circular copies around a center point inside a sketch.

| `type` | "circular" | Must be `'circular'` |
| `center` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The center point to copy around |
| `options` | CircularCopyOptions | Copy count, angle, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to copy (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
copy(type: "circular", axis: AxisLike, options: CircularCopyOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

[3D] Creates circular copies around an axis.

| `type` | "circular" | Must be `'circular'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The axis to copy around |
| `options` | CircularCopyOptions | Copy count, angle, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to copy (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

# ellipse()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/ellipse.mdx

sidebar_position: 4
title: "ellipse"
description: "Draws an ellipse at the current position."

# ellipse()

Draws an ellipse at the current position.

**Returns**: [**`ExtrudableGeometry`**](/docs/api/types/extrudable-geometry)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/sketching/primitive-shapes) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
ellipse(rx: NumberParam, ry: NumberParam): ExtrudableGeometry
```

Draws an ellipse at the current position.

| `rx` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's X axis |
| `ry` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's Y axis |

```ts
ellipse(center: Point2DLike, rx: NumberParam, ry: NumberParam): ExtrudableGeometry
```

Draws an ellipse at a given center.

| `center` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The center point |
| `rx` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's X axis |
| `ry` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's Y axis |

```ts
ellipse(targetPlane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, rx: NumberParam, ry: NumberParam): ExtrudableGeometry
```

Draws an ellipse on a specific plane.

| `targetPlane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to draw on |
| `rx` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's X axis |
| `ry` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's Y axis |

```ts
ellipse(targetPlane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, center: Point2DLike, rx: NumberParam, ry: NumberParam): ExtrudableGeometry
```

Draws an ellipse at a given center on a specific plane.

| `targetPlane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to draw on |
| `center` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The center point in plane-local coordinates |
| `rx` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's X axis |
| `ry` | NumberParam | Semi-radius along the plane's Y axis |

sidebar_position: 18
title: "pMove"
description: "Moves the cursor by polar coordinates, relative to the current tangent. The angle is measured from the tangent of the previous geometry (defaults to +X when there is none)."

# pMove()

Moves the cursor by polar coordinates, relative to the current tangent.
The angle is measured from the tangent of the previous geometry (defaults to +X
when there is none).

**Returns**: [**`Geometry`**](/docs/api/types/geometry)

## Signatures

```ts
pMove(radius: number, angle: number): Geometry
```

Moves the cursor by polar coordinates, relative to the current tangent.
The angle is measured from the tangent of the previous geometry (defaults to +X
when there is none).

| `radius` | number | The distance to move |
| `angle` | number | The angle in degrees, relative to the current tangent |

```ts
pMove(target: SceneObject, angle: number): Geometry
```

Moves the cursor along the given angle (relative to the current tangent) to the
nearest intersection with the target geometry. The nearest intersection (in either
direction along the ray) is used.

| `target` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The geometry to intersect with |
| `angle` | number | The angle in degrees, relative to the current tangent |

# tArc()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/tArc.mdx

sidebar_position: 21
title: "tArc"
description: "Draws a tangent arc from the current position using the current tangent direction, ending tangent to a target line. The radius is solved automatically; the arc must be tangent to the target but does not need to touch its finite extent. By default the arc curves to the left of the start tangent — chain `.flip()` to curve to the right instead."

# tArc()

Draws a tangent arc from the current position using the current tangent
direction, ending tangent to a target line. The radius is solved
automatically; the arc must be tangent to the target but does not need
to touch its finite extent. By default the arc curves to the left of
the start tangent — chain `.flip()` to curve to the right instead.

**Returns**: [**`Geometry`**](/docs/api/types/geometry)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/sketching/constrained-geometry) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
tArc(target: SceneObject | QualifiedGeometry): ITangentArcToObject
```

Draws a tangent arc from the current position using the current tangent
direction, ending tangent to a target line. The radius is solved
automatically; the arc must be tangent to the target but does not need
to touch its finite extent. By default the arc curves to the left of
the start tangent — chain `.flip()` to curve to the right instead.

| `target` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| QualifiedGeometry | The target line (or a qualified line) |

```ts
tArc(radius: number, target: SceneObject | QualifiedGeometry): Geometry
```

Draws a tangent arc from the current position using the current tangent
direction, with the given radius, ending at the first intersection with
the target geometry along the arc's sweep direction. A negative radius
flips the sweep direction. Supported targets: lines, circles, and arcs.

| `radius` | number | The arc radius. A negative value flips the sweep direction. |
| `target` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| QualifiedGeometry | The target geometry to intersect with |

```ts
tArc(radius?: number, endAngle?: number): Geometry
```

Draws a tangent arc with a given radius and end angle.

| `radius` | number | The arc radius (defaults to 100). A negative value flips the sweep direction. *(optional)* |
| `endAngle` | number | The sweep angle in degrees (defaults to 90) *(optional)* |

```ts
tArc(radius: number, angle: number, tangent: Point2DLike): Geometry
```

Draws a tangent arc with a given radius, angle, and start tangent direction.

| `radius` | number | The arc radius. A negative value flips the sweep direction. |
| `angle` | number | The sweep angle in degrees |
| `tangent` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The start tangent direction |

```ts
tArc(endPoint: Point2DLike): Geometry
```

Draws a tangent arc to a given end point.

| `endPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end point of the arc |

```ts
tArc(endPoint: Point2DLike, tangent: Point2DLike): Geometry
```

Draws a tangent arc to a given end point with an explicit end tangent.

| `endPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end point of the arc |
| `tangent` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end tangent direction |

```ts
tArc(startPoint: Point2DLike, endPoint: Point2DLike, tangent: Point2DLike): Geometry
```

Draws a tangent arc from a start point to an end point with a tangent.

| `startPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The start point of the arc |
| `endPoint` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end point of the arc |
| `tangent` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The end tangent direction |

```ts
tArc(c1: SceneObject, c2: SceneObject, radius: number, mustTouch?: boolean): TangentArcTwoObjects
```

Draws all possible tangent arcs between two geometry objects.

| `c1` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The first geometry object |
| `c2` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The second geometry object |
| `radius` | number | The arc radius |
| `mustTouch` | boolean | Whether the arc must touch both objects *(optional)* |

```ts
tArc(c1: QualifiedGeometry, c2: QualifiedGeometry, radius: number, mustTouch?: boolean): TangentArcTwoObjects
```

Draws a tangent arc between two qualified geometry objects.

| `c1` | QualifiedGeometry | The first qualified geometry object (e.g., `outside(circle1)`) |
| `c2` | QualifiedGeometry | The second qualified geometry object |
| `radius` | number | The arc radius |
| `mustTouch` | boolean | Whether the arc must touch both objects *(optional)* |

```ts
tArc(c1: Point2DLike, c2: Point2DLike, radius: number, mustTouch?: boolean): TangentArcTwoObjects
```

Draws a tangent arc between two points.

| `c1` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The first point |
| `c2` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) | The second point |
| `radius` | number | The arc radius |
| `mustTouch` | boolean | Whether the arc must touch both points *(optional)* |

```ts
tArc(c1: Point2DLike | SceneObject | QualifiedGeometry, c2: Point2DLike | SceneObject | QualifiedGeometry, radius: number, mustTouch?: boolean): TangentArcTwoObjects
```

Draws a tangent arc using a mix of geometry objects, qualified objects, or points as constraints.

| `c1` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) \| [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| QualifiedGeometry | The first constraint object or point |
| `c2` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) \| [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| QualifiedGeometry | The second constraint object or point |
| `radius` | number | The arc radius |
| `mustTouch` | boolean | Whether the arc must touch both constraints *(optional)* |

---

# text()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/2d/text.mdx

sidebar_position: 9
title: "text"
description: "Renders a text string as extrudable outline geometry inside the current sketch, at the sketch cursor."

import text_alignExample from '!!raw-loader!../../_examples/text-align.js';
import text_basicExample from '!!raw-loader!../../_examples/text-basic.js';
import text_fontExample from '!!raw-loader!../../_examples/text-font.js';
import text_pathExample from '!!raw-loader!../../_examples/text-path.js';
import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';

# text()

Renders a text string as extrudable outline geometry inside the current
sketch, at the sketch cursor.

**Returns**: [**`Text`**](/docs/api/types/text)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/sketching/compound-shapes) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
text(text: string): Text
```

Renders a text string as extrudable outline geometry inside the current
sketch, at the sketch cursor.

| `text` | string | The string to render. |

```ts
text(plane: SceneObject | PlaneLike, text: string): Text
```

Renders a text string on a specific plane (standalone, outside a sketch).

| `plane` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) \| [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane (e.g. "xy") or face to render the text on. |
| `text` | string | The string to render. |

```ts
text(text: string, path: SceneObject): Text
```

Renders a text string following a planar curve. Each glyph is placed
upright along the path's arc length; the text plane is the path's plane.
Works inside a sketch (following a curve of that sketch) or standalone.
The path is left in place — mark it `.guide()` to keep it out of
extruded profiles.

| `text` | string | The string to render. |
| `path` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The curve to follow: a sketch curve (line/arc/circle), a whole sketch, a planar primitive, or a selected edge/edge loop (e.g. `select(edge().circle())`). |

## Examples

<CodeBlock language="js">{text_basicExample}</CodeBlock>

![text example](/img/docs/api/text-basic.png)

<CodeBlock language="js">{text_fontExample}</CodeBlock>

![text example](/img/docs/api/text-font.png)

<CodeBlock language="js">{text_pathExample}</CodeBlock>

![text example](/img/docs/api/text-path.png)

# fillet()

Fillets selected edges with the given radius.

See the [guide](/docs/guides/3d-operations/fillet) for detailed usage examples.

## Signatures

```ts
fillet(radius?: NumberParam): SceneObject
```

Fillets selected edges with the given radius.

| `radius` | NumberParam | The fillet radius (defaults to 1) *(optional)* |

```ts

```

Fillets the given edge selections with the given radius.

| `radius` | NumberParam | The fillet radius |
| `...sceneObjects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The edge selections to fillet *(optional)* |

```ts
fillet(objects: Geometry[]): SceneObject
```

[2D] Fillets corners between the given geometries.

| `objects` | [Geometry](/docs/api/types/geometry)[] | The geometries whose corners to fillet |

```ts
fillet(objects: Geometry[], radius: NumberParam): SceneObject
```

[2D] Fillets corners between the given geometries with a radius.

| `objects` | [Geometry](/docs/api/types/geometry)[] | The geometries whose corners to fillet |
| `radius` | NumberParam | The fillet radius |

```ts
fillet(radius: NumberParam, ...objects: Geometry[]): SceneObject
```

[2D] Fillets corners at the given radius and geometries.

| `radius` | NumberParam | The fillet radius |
| `...objects` | [Geometry](/docs/api/types/geometry)[] | The geometries whose corners to fillet *(optional)* |

# helix()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/3d/helix.mdx

sidebar_position: 18
title: "helix"
description: "Creates a helix wire along the given axis. Use chained methods (.pitch(), .turns(), .height(), .radius(), .endRadius()) to configure geometry."

import helix_basicExample from '!!raw-loader!../../_examples/helix-basic.js';
import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';

# helix()

Creates a helix wire along the given axis. Use chained methods (.pitch(),
.turns(), .height(), .radius(), .endRadius()) to configure geometry.

**Returns**: [**`Helix`**](/docs/api/types/helix)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/3d-operations/helix) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
helix(axis: AxisLike): Helix
```

Creates a helix wire along the given axis. Use chained methods (.pitch(),
.turns(), .height(), .radius(), .endRadius()) to configure geometry.

| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The axis to build the helix around. |

```ts
helix(source: SceneObject): Helix
```

Creates a helix wire derived from a scene object's geometry.
- A cylindrical or conical face: axis + radii + height come from the face.
- A line edge: axis = the line, height = line length.
- A circular edge: axis = circle normal at center, radius = circle radius.

| `source` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The scene object whose face/edge defines the helix. |

## Examples

<CodeBlock language="js">{helix_basicExample}</CodeBlock>

![helix example](/img/docs/api/helix-basic.png)

# wrap()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/3d/wrap.mdx

sidebar_position: 17
title: "wrap"
description: "Wraps the given sketch onto a curved face, raising it from the surface by the given thickness (emboss). Chain `.remove()` to sink it into the surface instead (deboss), or `.new()` to keep the wrapped pad standalone. The sketch is developed onto the surface with its lengths preserved — a true wrap, not a projection. Cylindrical and conical faces are supported."

import wrap_basicExample from '!!raw-loader!../../_examples/wrap-basic.js';
import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';

# wrap()

Wraps the given sketch onto a curved face, raising it from the surface by
the given thickness (emboss). Chain `.remove()` to sink it into the
surface instead (deboss), or `.new()` to keep the wrapped pad standalone.
The sketch is developed onto the surface with its lengths preserved — a
true wrap, not a projection. Cylindrical and conical faces are supported.

**Returns**: [**`Wrap`**](/docs/api/types/wrap)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/3d-operations/wrap) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
wrap(thickness: NumberParam, sketch: SceneObject, face: SceneObject): Wrap
```

Wraps the given sketch onto a curved face, raising it from the surface by
the given thickness (emboss). Chain `.remove()` to sink it into the
surface instead (deboss), or `.new()` to keep the wrapped pad standalone.
The sketch is developed onto the surface with its lengths preserved — a
true wrap, not a projection. Cylindrical and conical faces are supported.

| `thickness` | NumberParam | Pad thickness measured along the surface normal (must be positive) |
| `sketch` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The sketch to wrap onto the face |
| `face` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The target face to wrap onto |

## Examples

<CodeBlock language="js">{wrap_basicExample}</CodeBlock>

![wrap example](/img/docs/api/wrap-basic.png)

---

# repeat()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/transforms/repeat.mdx

sidebar_position: 5
title: "repeat"
description: "Creates linear repeated instances along an axis."

# repeat()

Creates linear repeated instances along an axis.

**Returns**: [**`SceneObject`**](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/patterns) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
repeat(type: "linear", axis: AxisLike, options: LinearRepeatOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

Creates linear repeated instances along an axis.

| `type` | "linear" | Must be `'linear'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The axis to repeat along |
| `options` | [LinearRepeatOptions](/docs/api/types/linear-repeat-options) | Repeat count, spacing, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to repeat (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
repeat(type: "linear", axis: AxisLike[], options: LinearRepeatOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

Creates linear repeated instances along multiple axes.

| `type` | "linear" | Must be `'linear'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like)[] | The axes to repeat along |
| `options` | [LinearRepeatOptions](/docs/api/types/linear-repeat-options) | Repeat count, spacing, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to repeat (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

#### LinearRepeatOptions

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `count` | number \| number[] | Number of instances per axis (including the original) |
| `offset` | number \| number[] | Spacing between each instance. Cannot be used with `length`. *(optional)* |
| `length` | number \| number[] | Total span to distribute instances across (evenly spaced). Cannot be used with `offset`. *(optional)* |
| `centered` | boolean | When `true`, centers the pattern around the original object's position *(optional)* |
| `skip` | number[][] | Index tuples to skip (e.g. `[[1], [3]]` for single axis, `[[1, 2]]` for multi-axis) *(optional)* |

```ts
repeat(type: "circular", axis: AxisLike, options: CircularRepeatOptions, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

Creates circular repeated instances around an axis.

| `type` | "circular" | Must be `'circular'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The axis to repeat around |
| `options` | [CircularRepeatOptions](/docs/api/types/circular-repeat-options) | Repeat count, angle, etc. |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to repeat (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

#### CircularRepeatOptions

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `count` | number | Number of instances (including the original) |
| `angle` | number | Total angle to spread across. Cannot be used with `offset`. *(optional)* |
| `offset` | number | Angle between each instance. Cannot be used with `angle`. *(optional)* |
| `centered` | boolean | When `true`, centers the pattern around the original object's position *(optional)* |
| `skip` | number[] | Indices to skip (e.g. `[2, 4]` to skip the 3rd and 5th instances) *(optional)* |

```ts
repeat(type: "mirror", plane: PlaneLike, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

Creates a mirrored instance of objects across a plane.

| `type` | "mirror" | Must be `'mirror'` |
| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The plane to mirror across |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to mirror (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
repeat(type: "rotate", axis: AxisLike, angle?: NumberParam, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

Creates a rotated clone of objects around an axis.

| `type` | "rotate" | Must be `'rotate'` |
| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The axis to rotate around |
| `angle` | NumberParam | The rotation angle in degrees (defaults to 90) *(optional)* |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to rotate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
repeat(matrix: Matrix4, ...objects: SceneObject[]): SceneObject
```

Creates a transformed clone of objects using an arbitrary matrix.

| `matrix` | Matrix4 | The transformation matrix to apply |
| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to transform (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

---

# translate()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/transforms/translate.mdx

sidebar_position: 1
title: "translate"
description: "Translates objects along the X axis."

# translate()

Translates objects along the X axis.

**Returns**: [**`SceneObject`**](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

:::tip
See the [guide](/docs/guides/transforms) for detailed usage examples.
:::

## Signatures

```ts
translate(x: NumberParam, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects along the X axis.

| `x` | NumberParam | The X distance |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
translate(x: NumberParam, copy: BooleanParam, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects along the X axis, optionally making a copy.

| `x` | NumberParam | The X distance |
| `copy` | BooleanParam | Whether to copy instead of move |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
translate(x: NumberParam, y: NumberParam, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects along the X and Y axes.

| `x` | NumberParam | The X distance |
| `y` | NumberParam | The Y distance |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
translate(x: NumberParam, y: NumberParam, copy: BooleanParam, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects along the X and Y axes, optionally making a copy.

| `x` | NumberParam | The X distance |
| `y` | NumberParam | The Y distance |
| `copy` | BooleanParam | Whether to copy instead of move |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
translate(x: NumberParam, y: NumberParam, z: NumberParam, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects along all three axes.

| `x` | NumberParam | The X distance |
| `y` | NumberParam | The Y distance |
| `z` | NumberParam | The Z distance |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
translate(x: NumberParam, y: NumberParam, z: NumberParam, copy: BooleanParam, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects along all three axes, optionally making a copy.

| `x` | NumberParam | The X distance |
| `y` | NumberParam | The Y distance |
| `z` | NumberParam | The Z distance |
| `copy` | BooleanParam | Whether to copy instead of move |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
translate(distance: PointLike, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects by a point-like offset.

| `distance` | [PointLike](/docs/api/types/point-like) | The offset as a point |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

```ts
translate(distance: PointLike, copy: boolean, ...targets: SceneObject[]): ITranslate
```

Translates objects by a point-like offset, optionally making a copy.

| `distance` | [PointLike](/docs/api/types/point-like) | The offset as a point |
| `copy` | boolean | Whether to copy instead of move |
| `...targets` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The objects to translate (defaults to last object) *(optional)* |

---

# axis()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/utilities/axis.mdx

sidebar_position: 5
title: "axis"
description: "Creates an axis from a direction vector."

# axis()

Creates an axis from a direction vector.

**Returns**: [**`Axis`**](/docs/api/types/axis)

## Signatures

```ts
axis(axis: AxisLike): Axis
```

Creates an axis from a direction vector.

| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The direction vector or standard axis |

```ts
axis(axis: AxisLike, options: AxisTransformOptions): Axis
```

Creates an axis from a direction vector with transform options.

| `axis` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The direction vector or standard axis |
| `options` | AxisTransformOptions | Transform options (offset, flip, etc.) |

```ts
axis(source: SceneObject): Axis
```

Creates an axis from a scene object's edge.

| `source` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The scene object whose edge defines the axis |

```ts
axis(source: SceneObject, options: AxisTransformOptions): Axis
```

Creates an axis from a scene object's edge with transform options.

| `source` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The scene object whose edge defines the axis |
| `options` | AxisTransformOptions | Transform options (offset, flip, etc.) |

```ts
axis(axis: Axis, options: AxisTransformOptions): Axis
```

Transforms an existing axis with options.

| `axis` | [Axis](/docs/api/types/axis) | The existing axis to transform |
| `options` | AxisTransformOptions | Transform options (offset, flip, etc.) |

```ts
axis(a1: AxisLike, a2: AxisLike, options?: AxisTransformOptions): Axis
```

Creates an axis midway between two direction vectors.

| `a1` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The first direction vector or standard axis |
| `a2` | [AxisLike](/docs/api/types/axis-like) | The second direction vector or standard axis |
| `options` | AxisTransformOptions | Transform options (offset, flip, etc.) *(optional)* |

```ts
axis(a1: Axis, a2: Axis, options?: AxisTransformOptions): Axis
```

Creates an axis midway between two existing Axis objects.

| `a1` | [Axis](/docs/api/types/axis) | The first Axis object |
| `a2` | [Axis](/docs/api/types/axis) | The second Axis object |
| `options` | AxisTransformOptions | Transform options (offset, flip, etc.) *(optional)* |

# plane()

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/features/utilities/plane.mdx

sidebar_position: 6
title: "plane"
description: "Creates a plane with transform options."

# plane()

Creates a plane with transform options.

**Returns**: [**`Plane`**](/docs/api/types/plane)

## Signatures

```ts
plane(plane: PlaneLike, options: PlaneTransformOptions): Plane
```

Creates a plane with transform options.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The standard plane or normal vector |
| `options` | [PlaneTransformOptions](/docs/api/types/plane-transform-options) | Transform options (offset, rotate, etc.) |

#### PlaneTransformOptions

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `offset` | number | Distance to translate the plane along its normal *(optional)* |
| `rotateX` | number | Rotation around the plane's X axis (in degrees) *(optional)* |
| `rotateY` | number | Rotation around the plane's Y axis (in degrees) *(optional)* |
| `rotateZ` | number | Rotation around the plane's Z axis / normal (in degrees) *(optional)* |

```ts
plane(plane: PlaneLike, offset: number): Plane
```

Creates a plane with an offset.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The standard plane or normal vector |
| `offset` | number | The offset distance |

```ts
plane(selection: SceneObject): Plane
```

Creates a plane from a selection. A selected face yields that face's
plane; a selected edge yields a plane at the edge start, oriented normal
to the edge and facing outward (away from the edge body), like a start cap.

| `selection` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The selected face or edge to create a plane from |

```ts
plane(selection: SceneObject, options: PlaneTransformOptions): Plane
```

Creates a plane from a face selection with transform options.

| `selection` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The selected face to create a plane from |
| `options` | [PlaneTransformOptions](/docs/api/types/plane-transform-options) | Transform options (offset, rotate, etc.) |

```ts
plane(selection: SceneObject, offsetOrPosition: number): Plane
```

Creates a plane from a selection with a numeric second argument. For a
face, the number is the offset distance along the face normal. For an
edge, it is a normalized position from `0` (start) to `1` (end), and the
plane is created at that point oriented normal to the edge. The normal
follows the edge's forward direction, except at the start (`0`) where it
faces outward (away from the edge body), so both ends read like caps.

| `selection` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The selected face or edge |
| `offsetOrPosition` | number | Face: offset distance. Edge: normalized 0–1 position. |

```ts
plane(edge: SceneObject, position: "start" | "middle" | "end"): Plane
```

Creates a plane at a named position along an edge, oriented normal to the
edge. At `'start'` the normal faces outward (away from the edge body);
`'middle'` and `'end'` follow the edge's forward direction.

| `edge` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | The selected edge |
| `position` | "start" \| "middle" \| "end" | `'start'`, `'middle'`, or `'end'` |

```ts
plane(plane: Plane, options: PlaneTransformOptions): Plane
```

Transforms an existing plane with options.

| `plane` | [Plane](/docs/api/types/plane) | The existing plane to transform |
| `options` | [PlaneTransformOptions](/docs/api/types/plane-transform-options) | Transform options (offset, rotate, etc.) |

```ts
plane(p1: PlaneLike, p2: PlaneLike, options?: PlaneTransformOptions): Plane
```

Creates a plane midway between two standard planes or normal vectors.

| `p1` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The first standard plane or normal vector |
| `p2` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The second standard plane or normal vector |
| `options` | [PlaneTransformOptions](/docs/api/types/plane-transform-options) | Transform options (offset, rotate, etc.) *(optional)* |

```ts
plane(p1: Plane, p2: Plane, options?: PlaneTransformOptions): Plane
```

Creates a plane midway between two existing Plane objects.

| `p1` | [Plane](/docs/api/types/plane) | The first Plane object |
| `p2` | [Plane](/docs/api/types/plane) | The second Plane object |
| `options` | [PlaneTransformOptions](/docs/api/types/plane-transform-options) | Transform options (offset, flip, sticky, etc.) *(optional)* |

:::note
All signatures also accept an optional `targetPlane` parameter as the last argument to draw on a specific plane.
:::

# EdgeFilter

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/filters/edge-filter.mdx

sidebar_position: 2
title: "EdgeFilter"
description: "Creates a new edge filter builder for selecting edges by geometric properties."

# EdgeFilter

Creates a new edge filter builder for selecting edges by geometric properties.

```ts
import { edge } from 'fluidcad/filters';
```

## Methods

### .onPlane()

```ts
.onPlane(plane: PlaneLike, offsetOrOptions?: number | { offset?: number; bothDirections?: boolean; partial?: boolean; }): this
```

Selects edges that lie on the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offsetOrOptions` | `number \| { offset?: number; bothDirections?: boolean; partial?: boolean; }` | Offset distance, or an options object with `offset`, `bothDirections`, and `partial`. *(optional)* |

### .notOnPlane()

```ts
.notOnPlane(plane: PlaneLike, offsetOrOptions?: number | { offset?: number; bothDirections?: boolean; partial?: boolean; }): this
```

Excludes edges that lie on the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offsetOrOptions` | `number \| { offset?: number; bothDirections?: boolean; partial?: boolean; }` | Offset distance, or an options object with `offset`, `bothDirections`, and `partial`. *(optional)* |

### .parallelTo()

```ts
.parallelTo(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Selects edges that are parallel to the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |

### .notParallelTo()

```ts
.notParallelTo(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Excludes edges that are parallel to the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |

### .verticalTo()

```ts
.verticalTo(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Selects edges that are perpendicular (vertical) to the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |

### .notVerticalTo()

```ts
.notVerticalTo(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Excludes edges that are perpendicular (vertical) to the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |

### .circle()

```ts
.circle(diameter?: number): this
```

Selects circular edges, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to match. *(optional)* |

### .notCircle()

```ts
.notCircle(diameter?: number): this
```

Excludes circular edges, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to exclude. *(optional)* |

### .arc()

```ts
.arc(radius?: number): this
```

Selects arc edges, optionally matching a specific radius.

| `radius` | number | Optional radius to match. *(optional)* |

### .notArc()

```ts
.notArc(radius?: number): this
```

Excludes arc edges, optionally matching a specific radius.

| `radius` | number | Optional radius to exclude. *(optional)* |

### .line()

```ts
.line(length?: number): this
```

Selects straight-line edges, optionally matching a specific length.

| `length` | number | Optional length to match. *(optional)* |

### .notLine()

```ts
.notLine(length?: number): this
```

Excludes straight-line edges, optionally matching a specific length.

| `length` | number | Optional length to exclude. *(optional)* |

### .belongsToFace()

```ts
.belongsToFace(...args: any[][]): this
```

| `...args` | any[] |  *(optional)* |

### .notBelongsToFace()

```ts
.notBelongsToFace(...args: any[][]): this
```

| `...args` | any[] |  *(optional)* |

### .intersectsWith()

```ts
.intersectsWith(sceneObject: SceneObject): this
```

Selects edges that geometrically intersect with edges of the given scene object.

| `sceneObject` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | A scene object whose edges are tested for intersection. |

### .notIntersectsWith()

```ts
.notIntersectsWith(sceneObject: SceneObject): this
```

Excludes edges that geometrically intersect with edges of the given scene object.

| `sceneObject` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | A scene object whose edges are tested for intersection. |

### .above()

```ts
.above(plane: PlaneLike, offsetOrOptions?: number | { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }): this
```

Selects edges that are entirely above the given plane (in the direction of its normal).

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offsetOrOptions` | `number \| { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }` | Offset distance, or an options object with `offset` and `partial`. *(optional)* |

### .below()

```ts
.below(plane: PlaneLike, offsetOrOptions?: number | { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }): this
```

Selects edges that are entirely below the given plane (opposite to its normal direction).

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offsetOrOptions` | `number \| { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }` | Offset distance, or an options object with `offset` and `partial`. *(optional)* |

### .from()

```ts
.from(...sceneObjects: SceneObject[][]): this
```

Restricts the selection to edges originating from the given scene objects.
Recursive: passing a container picks up edges from its descendants.

| `...sceneObjects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | Scene objects whose edges (and edges of their sub-shapes) are matched against. *(optional)* |

---

# FaceFilter

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/filters/face-filter.mdx

sidebar_position: 1
title: "FaceFilter"
description: "Creates a new face filter builder for selecting faces by geometric properties."

# FaceFilter

Creates a new face filter builder for selecting faces by geometric properties.

```ts
import { face } from 'fluidcad/filters';
```

## Methods

### .onPlane()

```ts
.onPlane(plane: PlaneLike, offset?: number): this
```

Selects faces that lie on the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offset` | number | Optional distance to offset the plane before matching. *(optional)* |

### .notOnPlane()

```ts
.notOnPlane(plane: PlaneLike, offset?: number): this
```

Excludes faces that lie on the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offset` | number | Optional distance to offset the plane before matching. *(optional)* |

### .circle()

```ts
.circle(diameter?: number): this
```

Selects circular (flat, disc-shaped) faces, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to match. *(optional)* |

### .notCircle()

```ts
.notCircle(diameter?: number): this
```

Excludes circular (flat, disc-shaped) faces, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to exclude. *(optional)* |

### .cylinder()

```ts
.cylinder(diameter?: number): this
```

Selects cylindrical faces, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to match. *(optional)* |

### .notCylinder()

```ts
.notCylinder(diameter?: number): this
```

Excludes cylindrical faces, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to exclude. *(optional)* |

### .cylinderCurve()

```ts
.cylinderCurve(diameter?: number): this
```

Selects faces bounded by cylindrical curves, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to match. *(optional)* |

### .notCylinderCurve()

```ts
.notCylinderCurve(diameter?: number): this
```

Excludes faces bounded by cylindrical curves, optionally matching a specific diameter.

| `diameter` | number | Optional diameter to exclude. *(optional)* |

### .parallelTo()

```ts
.parallelTo(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Selects faces whose normal is parallel to the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |

### .notParallelTo()

```ts
.notParallelTo(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Excludes faces whose normal is parallel to the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |

### .torus()

```ts
.torus(majorRadius?: number, minorRadius?: number): this
```

Selects toroidal faces, optionally matching major and/or minor radius.

| `majorRadius` | number | Optional radius from the torus axis to the tube center. *(optional)* |
| `minorRadius` | number | Optional radius of the tube itself. *(optional)* |

### .notTorus()

```ts
.notTorus(majorRadius?: number, minorRadius?: number): this
```

Excludes toroidal faces, optionally matching major and/or minor radius.

| `majorRadius` | number | Optional radius from the torus axis to the tube center. *(optional)* |
| `minorRadius` | number | Optional radius of the tube itself. *(optional)* |

### .planar()

```ts
.planar(): this
```

Selects planar (flat) faces.

### .notPlanar()

```ts
.notPlanar(): this
```

Excludes planar (flat) faces.

### .cone()

```ts
.cone(): this
```

Selects conical faces.

### .notCone()

```ts
.notCone(): this
```

Excludes conical faces.

### .intersectsWith()

```ts
.intersectsWith(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Selects faces that intersect with the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane to test intersection against. |

### .notIntersectsWith()

```ts
.notIntersectsWith(plane: PlaneLike): this
```

Excludes faces that intersect with the given plane.

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane to test intersection against. |

### .hasEdge()

```ts
.hasEdge(...args: any[][]): this
```

| `...args` | any[] |  *(optional)* |

### .notHasEdge()

```ts
.notHasEdge(...args: any[][]): this
```

| `...args` | any[] |  *(optional)* |

### .edgeCount()

```ts
.edgeCount(count: number): this
```

Selects faces with exactly the given number of edges.

| `count` | number | The exact number of edges to match. |

### .notEdgeCount()

```ts
.notEdgeCount(count: number): this
```

Excludes faces with the given number of edges.

| `count` | number | The number of edges to exclude. |

### .above()

```ts
.above(plane: PlaneLike, offsetOrOptions?: number | { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }): this
```

Selects faces that are entirely above the given plane (in the direction of its normal).

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offsetOrOptions` | `number \| { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }` | Offset distance, or an options object with `offset` and `partial`. *(optional)* |

### .below()

```ts
.below(plane: PlaneLike, offsetOrOptions?: number | { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }): this
```

Selects faces that are entirely below the given plane (opposite to its normal direction).

| `plane` | [PlaneLike](/docs/api/types/plane-like) | The reference plane. |
| `offsetOrOptions` | `number \| { offset?: number; partial?: boolean; }` | Offset distance, or an options object with `offset` and `partial`. *(optional)* |

### .from()

```ts
.from(...sceneObjects: SceneObject[][]): this
```

Restricts the selection to faces originating from the given scene objects.
Recursive: passing a container picks up faces from its descendants.

| `...sceneObjects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | Scene objects whose faces (and faces of their sub-shapes) are matched against. *(optional)* |

---

# API Reference

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/index.mdx

sidebar_position: 0
title: "API Reference"
description: "FluidCAD API Reference - complete documentation for all features, types, and filters."
slug: "/api"

# API Reference

Complete API documentation for FluidCAD.

## Features

Functions for creating and manipulating geometry.

- **2D Sketching** - Lines, circles, arcs, rectangles, and other 2D geometry
- **3D Operations** - Extrude, revolve, loft, sweep, booleans, and modifications
- **Transforms** - Translate, rotate, mirror, copy, and repeat
- **Utilities** - Select, color, remove, load, and other utilities

## Types

Return types from feature functions. These provide methods for further operations on created geometry.

- [**SceneObject**](/docs/api/types/scene-object) - Base type for all scene objects
- [**Extrude**](/docs/api/types/extrude) - Return type for `extrude()`
- [**Revolve**](/docs/api/types/revolve) - Return type for `revolve()`
- [**Loft**](/docs/api/types/loft) - Return type for `loft()`
- [**Sweep**](/docs/api/types/sweep) - Return type for `sweep()`

## Filters

Filter builders for selecting specific faces and edges.

- [**FaceFilter**](/docs/api/filters/face-filter) - Filter faces by shape, plane, and orientation
- [**EdgeFilter**](/docs/api/filters/edge-filter) - Filter edges by curve type, plane, and orientation

## Constraints

Constraint qualifiers for tangent geometry.

- [**Constraints**](/docs/api/constraints) - `outside()`, `enclosed()`, `enclosing()`, `unqualified()`

---

# ALine

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/aline.mdx

sidebar_position: 16.5
title: "ALine"
description: "The ALine type. Extends Geometry."

# ALine

Extends [`Geometry`](/docs/api/types/geometry)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`Geometry`](/docs/api/types/geometry)</summary>

### guide()

```ts
guide(): this
```

Marks this sketch geometry as construction geometry. Guide geometries are
excluded from the final sketch output (e.g., extrude, revolve) unless
explicitly included.

### start()

```ts
start(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the start point of this geometry element.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### end()

```ts
end(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the end point of this geometry element.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### tangent()

```ts
tangent(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex representing the tangent direction at the end
of this geometry. Used to determine the direction of subsequent geometry elements.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### centered()

```ts
centered(value?: boolean): this
```

Controls whether the line is centered on the current position.
When `true`, the line is offset backward by half its length so that the
current position falls at its midpoint.

| `value` | boolean | `true` to center, `false` (default) to start from the current position. *(optional)* |

---

# AxisLike

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/axis-like.mdx

sidebar_position: 26
title: "AxisLike"
description: "An axis reference accepted by revolve and other axis-based operations."

# AxisLike

An axis reference used by `revolve()` and other axis-based operations. Any of the following formats are accepted:

| Format | Example | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| Standard axis string | `"x"`, `"y"`, `"z"` | The three principal axes |
| [`Axis`](/docs/api/types/axis) | `axis("x", [0, 10])` | An axis object created with `axis()` |

---

# BooleanOperation

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/boolean-operation.mdx

sidebar_position: 3
title: "BooleanOperation"
description: "The BooleanOperation type. Extends SceneObject."

# BooleanOperation

Extends [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### add()

```ts
add(): this
```

Additive boolean operation — fuses the result with all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### 'new'()

```ts
'new'(): this
```

No boolean operation — keeps the result as a standalone shape,
separate from all other scene objects.

### remove()

```ts
remove(): this
```

Subtractive boolean operation — cuts the result from all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### scope()

```ts
scope(...objects: SceneObject[]): this
```

Narrows the boolean operation scope to specific target objects.
Must be chained after `.add()` or `.remove()`.

| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The target objects to operate on. *(optional)* |

---

# CircularRepeatOptions

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/circular-repeat-options.mdx

sidebar_position: 29
sidebar_label: "CircularRepeatOptions"
title: "CircularRepeatOptions"
description: "Options for circular repeat."

# CircularRepeatOptions

Options for [`repeat("circular", ...)`](/docs/api/features/transforms/repeat).

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `count` | number | Number of instances (including the original) |
| `angle` | number | Total angle to spread across. Cannot be used with `offset`. *(optional)* |
| `offset` | number | Angle between each instance. Cannot be used with `angle`. *(optional)* |
| `centered` | boolean | When `true`, centers the pattern around the original object's position *(optional)* |
| `skip` | number[] | Indices to skip (e.g. `[2, 4]` to skip the 3rd and 5th instances) *(optional)* |

---

# Cut

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/cut.mdx

sidebar_position: 7
title: "Cut"
description: "The Cut type. Extends SceneObject."

# Cut

Extends [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### symmetric()

```ts
symmetric(): this
```

Enables symmetric mode — cuts equally in both directions from the sketch plane.

### scope()

```ts
scope(...objects: SceneObject[]): this
```

Narrows the cut scope to specific target objects.
Must be chained after `.remove()`.

| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The target objects to cut from. *(optional)* |

### draft()

```ts
draft(value: NumberParam | [NumberParam, NumberParam]): this
```

Applies a draft (taper) angle to the cut walls.

| `value` | NumberParam \| [NumberParam, NumberParam] | A single angle for uniform draft, or a `[start, end]` tuple for asymmetric draft. |

### endOffset()

```ts
endOffset(value: NumberParam): this
```

Offsets the cut end face by a specified distance along the cut direction.

| `value` | NumberParam | The offset distance. |

### startEdges()

```ts
startEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges at the start of the cut path, classified by signed distance from the cut plane.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endEdges()

```ts
endEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges at the end of the cut path, classified by signed distance from the cut plane.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalEdges()

```ts
internalEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects internal edges created by the cut that are not on the cut plane boundary.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalFaces()

```ts
internalFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects internal faces exposed by the cut — newly created surfaces not from the original stock.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### pick()

```ts
pick(...points: Point2DLike[]): this
```

Restricts the cut to only the sketch regions containing the given points.

| `...points` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike)[] | 2D points in the sketch plane identifying regions to cut. *(optional)* |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin cut mode — offsets the profile edges to cut a thin-walled shape
instead of cutting filled faces. Positive values offset outward, negative values offset inward.

| `offset` | NumberParam | The wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset1: NumberParam, offset2: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin cut mode with two offset directions.
The two offsets must go in opposite directions. If both have the same sign,
the second offset is automatically flipped.

| `offset1` | NumberParam | The first wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |
| `offset2` | NumberParam | The second wall offset distance, in the opposite direction of offset1. |

---

## Methods

```ts
symmetric(): this
```

### startFaces()


**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### endFaces()

```ts
endFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces at the end (cap) of the extrusion.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### startEdges()

```ts
startEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the start (base) faces of the extrusion.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endEdges()

```ts
endEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideFaces()

```ts
sideFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the lateral faces created by the extrusion.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideEdges()

```ts

```

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalFaces()

```ts
internalFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces created inside the solid during extrusion (e.g., from holes or intersections).

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalEdges()

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capFaces()

```ts
capFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the cap faces at the open ends of a thin-walled extrusion from an open profile.
These are the small faces connecting the inner and outer walls at the profile endpoints.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capEdges()

```ts
capEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the cap faces of a thin-walled extrusion from an open profile.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### draft()

```ts
draft(value: NumberParam | [NumberParam, NumberParam]): this
```

Applies a draft (taper) angle to the extrusion walls.

| `value` | NumberParam \| [NumberParam, NumberParam] | A single angle for uniform draft, or a `[start, end]` tuple for asymmetric draft. |

### endOffset()

```ts
endOffset(value: NumberParam): this
```

Offsets the end face by a specified distance along the extrusion direction.

| `value` | NumberParam | The offset distance. |

### drill()

```ts
drill(value?: boolean): this
```

Enables or disables drill mode, which partitions the sketch into face regions
before extruding.

| `value` | boolean | `true` to enable (default), `false` to disable. *(optional)* |

### pick()

```ts
pick(...points: Point2DLike[]): this
```

Restricts extrusion to only the sketch regions containing the given points.

| `...points` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike)[] | 2D points in the sketch plane identifying regions to extrude. *(optional)* |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin extrude mode — offsets the profile edges to create a thin-walled solid
instead of extruding filled faces. Positive values offset outward, negative values offset inward.

| `offset` | NumberParam | The wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset1: NumberParam, offset2: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin extrude mode with two offset directions.
The two offsets must go in opposite directions. If both have the same sign,
the second offset is automatically flipped.

| `offset1` | NumberParam | The first wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |
| `offset2` | NumberParam | The second wall offset distance, in the opposite direction of offset1. |

---

# Geometry

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/geometry.mdx

sidebar_position: 4
title: "Geometry"
description: "The Geometry type. Extends SceneObject."

# Geometry

Extends [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### guide()

```ts
guide(): this
```

Marks this sketch geometry as construction geometry. Guide geometries are
excluded from the final sketch output (e.g., extrude, revolve) unless
explicitly included.

### start()
