
Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the start point of this geometry element.

### end()

```ts
end(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the end point of this geometry element.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### tangent()

```ts
tangent(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex representing the tangent direction at the end
of this geometry. Used to determine the direction of subsequent geometry elements.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

# Helix

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/helix.mdx

sidebar_position: 12.7
title: "Helix"
description: "The Helix type. Extends SceneObject."

# Helix

Extends [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### pitch()

```ts
pitch(pitch: number): this
```

Axial rise per turn (distance along the helix axis covered per full revolution).
If unset, derived from `height / turns`.

| `pitch` | number |  |

### turns()

```ts
turns(turns: number): this
```

Number of full turns. Fractional values are allowed. Default 1.

| `turns` | number |  |

### startOffset()

```ts
startOffset(offset: number): this
```

Shifts the start of the helix along its axis, in axial mm. Positive values
trim the start (move it toward the end); negative values extend it. Default 0.

| `offset` | number |  |

### endOffset()

```ts
endOffset(offset: number): this
```

Extends (positive) or trims (negative) the helix at its end, in axial mm.
Default 0.

| `offset` | number |  |

### height()

```ts
height(height: number): this
```

Total axial height. Overrides face/edge-derived height when set. For line-edge
input, defaults to the line length. For circular-edge / pure-axis input,
defaults to 50 if neither this nor `pitch * turns` determine it.

| `height` | number |  |

### radius()

```ts
radius(radius: number): this
```

Start radius. Defaults to 20 for axis/line-edge input. For a cylindrical
face input, defaults to the face's radius and may be overridden (useful for
sweep/fuse workflows where the helix tube must overlap the cylinder
volumetrically — offset by ~1mm to avoid pure tangency). Ignored on
conical face input (radius is derived from face geometry).

| `radius` | number |  |

### endRadius()

```ts
endRadius(radius: number): this
```

End radius — when different from `radius()`, produces a conical helix.
Defaults to `radius()`. Ignored on face/circle inputs.

| `radius` | number |  |

---

## Methods

### centered()

```ts
centered(value?: boolean): this
```

Controls whether the line is centered on the current position.
When `true`, the line is offset backward by half its length so that the
current position falls at its midpoint.

| `value` | boolean | `true` to center, `false` (default) to start from the current position. *(optional)* |

# LinearRepeatOptions

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/linear-repeat-options.mdx

sidebar_position: 28
sidebar_label: "LinearRepeatOptions"
title: "LinearRepeatOptions"
description: "Options for linear repeat."

# LinearRepeatOptions

Options for [`repeat("linear", ...)`](/docs/api/features/transforms/repeat).

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `count` | number \| number[] | Number of instances per axis (including the original) |
| `offset` | number \| number[] | Spacing between each instance. Cannot be used with `length`. *(optional)* |
| `length` | number \| number[] | Total span to distribute instances across (evenly spaced). Cannot be used with `offset`. *(optional)* |
| `centered` | boolean | When `true`, centers the pattern around the original object's position *(optional)* |
| `skip` | number[][] | Index tuples to skip (e.g. `[[1], [3]]` for single axis, `[[1, 2]]` for multi-axis) *(optional)* |

---

# Loft

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/loft.mdx

sidebar_position: 9
title: "Loft"
description: "The Loft type. Extends BooleanOperation."

# Loft

Extends [`BooleanOperation`](/docs/api/types/boolean-operation)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`BooleanOperation`](/docs/api/types/boolean-operation)</summary>

### add()

```ts
add(): this
```

Additive boolean operation — fuses the result with all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### 'new'()

```ts
'new'(): this
```

No boolean operation — keeps the result as a standalone shape,
separate from all other scene objects.

### remove()

```ts
remove(): this
```

Subtractive boolean operation — cuts the result from all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### scope()

```ts
scope(...objects: SceneObject[]): this
```

Narrows the boolean operation scope to specific target objects.
Must be chained after `.add()` or `.remove()`.

| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The target objects to operate on. *(optional)* |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### startFaces()

```ts
startFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces on the first profile plane of the loft.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endFaces()

```ts
endFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces on the last profile plane of the loft.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideFaces()

```ts
sideFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the lateral faces generated between loft profiles.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### startEdges()

```ts
startEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the first profile plane of the loft.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endEdges()

```ts
endEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the last profile plane of the loft.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideEdges()

```ts
sideEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the side faces, excluding edges shared with start/end faces.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin loft mode — offsets the profile edges of each section to create a
thin-walled shell instead of lofting filled faces. All profiles must be sketches
and share the same topology. Positive values offset outward, negative offsets inward.

| `offset` | NumberParam | The wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset1: NumberParam, offset2: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin loft mode with two offset directions.
The two offsets must go in opposite directions. If both have the same sign,
the second offset is automatically flipped.

| `offset1` | NumberParam | The first wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |
| `offset2` | NumberParam | The second wall offset distance, in the opposite direction of offset1. |

### internalFaces()

```ts
internalFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces created inside the solid during loft (e.g., the inner
wall of a thin-walled loft from closed profiles).

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalEdges()

```ts
internalEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges bounding the internal geometry created during loft.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capFaces()

```ts
capFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the cap faces at the open ends of a thin-walled loft from open profiles.
These are the small faces connecting the inner and outer walls at the profile endpoints.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capEdges()

```ts
capEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the cap faces of a thin-walled loft from open profiles.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

---

# PlaneLike

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/plane-like.mdx

sidebar_position: 25
title: "PlaneLike"
description: "A plane reference accepted by 3D operations and sketching functions."

# PlaneLike

A plane reference used by `sketch()`, filters, and other operations. Any of the following formats are accepted:

| Format | Example | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| Standard plane string | `"xy"`, `"xz"`, `"yz"` | The three principal planes |
| Negative plane string | `"-xy"`, `"-xz"`, `"-yz"` | Principal planes with flipped normals |
| Named plane string | `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"front"`, `"back"`, `"left"`, `"right"` | Descriptive aliases for the principal planes |
| [`Plane`](/docs/api/types/plane) | `plane("xy", 10)` | A plane object created with `plane()` |
| [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object) | A face selection | A planar face to use as reference |

---

# PlaneTransformOptions

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/plane-transform-options.mdx

sidebar_position: 30
sidebar_label: "PlaneTransformOptions"
title: "PlaneTransformOptions"
description: "Options for transforming a plane with offset and rotation."

# PlaneTransformOptions

Options accepted by [`plane()`](/docs/api/features/utilities/plane) to offset and rotate a plane relative to its own axes. Rotations are composed together and applied around the plane's origin (after the offset is applied), so the plane tilts in place rather than orbiting the world origin.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `offset` | number | Distance to translate the plane along its normal *(optional)* |
| `rotateX` | number | Rotation around the plane's X axis (in degrees) *(optional)* |
| `rotateY` | number | Rotation around the plane's Y axis (in degrees) *(optional)* |
| `rotateZ` | number | Rotation around the plane's Z axis / normal (in degrees) *(optional)* |

---

# PointLike

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/point-like.mdx

sidebar_position: 24
title: "PointLike"
description: "A 3D point accepted by translate and other 3D operations."

# PointLike

A 3D point used by operations like `translate()`. Any of the following formats are accepted:

| Format | Example | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `[number, number, number]` | `[10, 20, 30]` | Tuple of x, y, z coordinates |
| `{ x, y, z }` | `{ x: 10, y: 20, z: 30 }` | Object with x, y, z properties |

---

# Point2DLike

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/point2dlike.mdx

sidebar_position: 23
title: "Point2DLike"
description: "A 2D point accepted by sketching functions."

# Point2DLike

A 2D point used by all sketching functions. Any of the following formats are accepted:

| Format | Example | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `[number, number]` | `[10, 20]` | Tuple of x, y coordinates |
| `number[]` | `[10, 20]` | Array of x, y coordinates |
| `{ x, y }` | `{ x: 10, y: 20 }` | Object with x, y properties |
| [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex) | `line(...).end()` | A vertex returned by a geometry method |

---

to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### radius()

```ts
radius(...r: number[]): this
```

Sets corner radii for a rounded rectangle. Accepts 1–4 values
in order: `[bottomLeft, bottomRight, topRight, topLeft]`.
A single value applies to all corners.

| `...r` | number[] | One or more radius values. *(optional)* |

### centered()

```ts
centered(value?: boolean | "horizontal" | "vertical"): this
```

Controls how the rectangle is positioned relative to the current point.

| `value` | boolean \| "horizontal" \| "vertical" | `true` centers on both axes, `'horizontal'` or `'vertical'` centers on one axis, `false` (default) keeps the current point as the origin corner. *(optional)* |

### topEdge()

```ts
topEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the top straight edge of the rectangle.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### bottomEdge()

```ts
bottomEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the bottom straight edge of the rectangle.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### leftEdge()

```ts
leftEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the left straight edge of the rectangle.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### rightEdge()

```ts
rightEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the right straight edge of the rectangle.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### topLeftArcEdge()

```ts
topLeftArcEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the arc edge at the top-left corner. Only present when a radius is applied.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### topRightArcEdge()

```ts
topRightArcEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the arc edge at the top-right corner. Only present when a radius is applied.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### bottomLeftArcEdge()

```ts
bottomLeftArcEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the arc edge at the bottom-left corner. Only present when a radius is applied.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### bottomRightArcEdge()

```ts
bottomRightArcEdge(): SceneObject
```

Returns the arc edge at the bottom-right corner. Only present when a radius is applied.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

### topLeft()

```ts
topLeft(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the top-left corner.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### topRight()

```ts
topRight(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the top-right corner.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### bottomLeft()

```ts
bottomLeft(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the bottom-left corner.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### bottomRight()

```ts
bottomRight(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the bottom-right corner.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

# Revolve

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/revolve.mdx

sidebar_position: 8
title: "Revolve"
description: "The Revolve type. Extends BooleanOperation."

# Revolve

Extends [`BooleanOperation`](/docs/api/types/boolean-operation)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`BooleanOperation`](/docs/api/types/boolean-operation)</summary>

### add()

```ts
add(): this
```

Additive boolean operation — fuses the result with all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### 'new'()

```ts
'new'(): this
```

No boolean operation — keeps the result as a standalone shape,
separate from all other scene objects.

### remove()

```ts
remove(): this
```

Subtractive boolean operation — cuts the result from all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### scope()

```ts
scope(...objects: SceneObject[]): this
```

Narrows the boolean operation scope to specific target objects.
Must be chained after `.add()` or `.remove()`.

| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The target objects to operate on. *(optional)* |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### symmetric()

```ts
symmetric(): this
```

Enables symmetric mode — revolves equally in both directions from the sketch plane.

### pick()

```ts
pick(...points: Point2DLike[]): this
```

Restricts the revolve to only the sketch regions containing the given points.

| `...points` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike)[] | 2D points in the sketch plane identifying regions to revolve. *(optional)* |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin revolve mode — offsets the profile edges to create a thin-walled
solid of revolution instead of revolving filled faces. Positive values offset
outward, negative values offset inward.

| `offset` | NumberParam | The wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset1: NumberParam, offset2: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin revolve mode with two offset directions.
The two offsets must go in opposite directions. If both have the same sign,
the second offset is automatically flipped.

| `offset1` | NumberParam | The first wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |
| `offset2` | NumberParam | The second wall offset distance, in the opposite direction of offset1. |

### internalFaces()

```ts
internalFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces created inside the solid during revolution (e.g., the inner
wall of a thin-walled revolve from a closed profile).

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalEdges()

```ts
internalEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges bounding the internal geometry created during revolution.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capFaces()

```ts
capFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the cap faces at the open ends of a thin-walled revolve from an open profile.
These are the small faces connecting the inner and outer walls at the profile endpoints.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capEdges()

```ts
capEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the cap faces of a thin-walled revolve from an open profile.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

---

# Rib

Extends [`BooleanOperation`](/docs/api/types/boolean-operation)

<details>

### add()

```ts
add(): this
```

### 'new'()


Subtractive boolean operation — cuts the result from all intersecting scene objects.

### scope()

```ts

```

Narrows the boolean operation scope to specific target objects.

| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The target objects to operate on. *(optional)* |

</details>

## Methods

### startFaces()

```ts
startFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces at the start (base) of the rib — the profile face at the sketch plane.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endFaces()

```ts
endFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects faces at the end (top) of the rib — where the rib meets the boundary.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideFaces()

```ts
sideFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the lateral wall faces of the rib.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capFaces()

```ts
capFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the small cap faces at the spine endpoints.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### startEdges()

```ts
startEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the start faces.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endEdges()

```ts
endEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the end faces.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideEdges()

```ts
sideEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the side faces, excluding edges shared with start/end faces.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### capEdges()

```ts
capEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the cap faces.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### draft()

```ts
draft(value: NumberParam | [NumberParam, NumberParam]): this
```

Applies a draft (taper) angle to the rib walls.

| `value` | NumberParam \| [NumberParam, NumberParam] | A single angle for uniform draft, or a `[start, end]` tuple for asymmetric draft. |

### parallel()

```ts
parallel(): this
```

Switches the extrusion direction to parallel to the sketch plane
(perpendicular to the spine within the plane) instead of normal to it.

### extend()

```ts
extend(): this
```

Extends the rib's side faces at the spine endpoints outward to blend
with the target solids' walls.

Extends [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

```ts
reusable(): this
```

### internalFaces()

```ts
internalFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

# Slot

# Slot

Extends [`ExtrudableGeometry`](/docs/api/types/extrudable-geometry)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`Geometry`](/docs/api/types/geometry)</summary>

### guide()

```ts
guide(): this
```

Marks this sketch geometry as construction geometry. Guide geometries are
excluded from the final sketch output (e.g., extrude, revolve) unless
explicitly included.

### start()

```ts
start(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the start point of this geometry element.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### end()

```ts
end(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the end point of this geometry element.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### tangent()

```ts
tangent(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex representing the tangent direction at the end
of this geometry. Used to determine the direction of subsequent geometry elements.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### centered()

```ts
centered(value?: boolean): this
```

Controls whether the slot is centered on the current position.
When `true`, the slot is offset backward by half its length.

| `value` | boolean | `true` to center, `false` (default) to start from the current position. *(optional)* |

### rotate()

```ts
rotate(angle: NumberParam): this
```

Sets the rotation angle of the slot's primary axis.

| `angle` | NumberParam | Rotation in degrees. |

```ts
sideFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

```ts
startEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

```ts

```


### thin()

```ts
thin(offset: NumberParam): this
```

Enables thin sweep mode — offsets the profile edges to create a thin-walled
swept shell instead of sweeping filled faces. Positive values offset outward,
negative values offset inward.

| `offset` | NumberParam | The wall offset distance. Positive = outward, negative = inward. |

### thin()

```ts
thin(offset1: NumberParam, offset2: NumberParam): this
```


Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### start()

```ts
start(index?: number): Vertex
```

Returns the start vertex of the tangent arc.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

| `index` | number | Solution index when multiple tangent arcs exist (defaults to 0). *(optional)* |

### end()

```ts
end(index?: number): Vertex
```

Returns the end vertex of the tangent arc.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

| `index` | number | Solution index when multiple tangent arcs exist (defaults to 0). *(optional)* |

# Text

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/text.mdx

sidebar_position: 17.5
title: "Text"
description: "The Text type. Extends ExtrudableGeometry."

# Text

Extends [`ExtrudableGeometry`](/docs/api/types/extrudable-geometry)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`Geometry`](/docs/api/types/geometry)</summary>

### guide()

```ts
guide(): this
```

Marks this sketch geometry as construction geometry. Guide geometries are
excluded from the final sketch output (e.g., extrude, revolve) unless
explicitly included.

### start()

```ts
start(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the start point of this geometry element.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### end()

```ts
end(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex at the end point of this geometry element.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

### tangent()

```ts
tangent(): Vertex
```

Returns a lazy-evaluated vertex representing the tangent direction at the end
of this geometry. Used to determine the direction of subsequent geometry elements.

**Returns**: [`Vertex`](/docs/api/types/vertex)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### size()

```ts
size(value: number): this
```

Sets the text height (em size) in model units. Default 10.

| `value` | number | The em size. |

### font()

```ts
font(name: string): this
```

Sets the font. A name without a font extension (e.g. `"Arial"`) is resolved
to a system font; a value ending in `.ttf`/`.otf`/`.ttc`/`.woff` (e.g.
`"fonts/Brand.ttf"`) is loaded as a workspace-relative file. When omitted, a
default system font is used.

| `name` | string | A system family name or a workspace-relative font file path. |

### weight()

```ts
weight(value: string | number): this
```

Sets the font weight: a number (100–900) or a name such as `"regular"`,
`"medium"`, or `"bold"`. Resolves to the matching face (or the wght axis of a
variable font).

| `value` | string \| number | The weight as a number or name. |

### bold()

```ts
bold(): this
```

Shortcut for `weight(700)`.

### italic()

```ts
italic(value?: boolean): this
```

Renders the italic/oblique face of the font.

| `value` | boolean | Whether to use italic (defaults to true). *(optional)* |

### align()

```ts
align(value: "left" | "right" | "center" | "start" | "end" | "space-between" | "space-around"): this
```

Horizontal alignment of the text. For straight text it is relative to the
origin point; for text along a path it positions the run against the
path: `"start"` begins at the path's start, `"center"` centers on the
midpoint, `"end"` finishes at the path's end, `"space-between"` justifies
the glyphs evenly across the whole path, and `"space-around"` spreads
them with half a gap before the first glyph and after the last, like the
CSS flexbox value (both path text only). `"left"` and `"right"` are
synonyms of `"start"` and `"end"`.

| `value` | "left" \| "right" \| "center" \| "start" \| "end" \| "space-between" \| "space-around" | `"left"`/`"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"right"`/`"end"`, `"space-between"`, or `"space-around"`. |

### lineSpacing()

```ts
lineSpacing(value: number): this
```

Line-height multiplier for multi-line text (newlines in the string).

| `value` | number | Multiplier on the font's natural line height (default 1). |

### letterSpacing()

```ts
letterSpacing(value: number): this
```

Extra spacing added between glyphs, in model units (default 0).

| `value` | number | The additional advance per glyph. |

### offset()

```ts
offset(value: number): this
```

Shifts the baseline perpendicular to the path, in model units: positive
values move the text toward its "up" side, negative below the path.
Only applies to text following a path (`text(string, path)`).

| `value` | number | The perpendicular baseline shift. |

### flip()

```ts
flip(value?: boolean): this
```

Mirrors the text to the other side of the path, reversing the reading
direction. On a closed path (circle, loop) text sits on the outside by
default — `.flip()` moves it inside. On an open path it mirrors the text
below the curve. Only applies to text following a path.

| `value` | boolean | Whether to flip (defaults to true). *(optional)* |

### startAt()

```ts
startAt(distance: number): this
```

Shifts where the text starts along the path, as an arc-length distance
from the path's start (combines with `align()`). On a closed path the
text wraps around. Only applies to text following a path.

| `distance` | number | The arc-length shift in model units. |

---

# Vertex

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/vertex.mdx

sidebar_position: 27
title: "Vertex"
description: "A lazy-evaluated vertex representing a point on geometry."

# Vertex

A lazy-evaluated vertex representing a point on geometry. Vertices are returned by methods like `start()`, `end()`, and `tangent()` on [`Geometry`](/docs/api/types/geometry) types.

Vertices can be passed as a [`Point2DLike`](/docs/api/types/point2dlike) to any function that accepts a 2D point, allowing you to reference points on existing geometry.

---

# Wrap

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/api/types/wrap.mdx

sidebar_position: 12.6

# Wrap

Extends [`BooleanOperation`](/docs/api/types/boolean-operation)

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`BooleanOperation`](/docs/api/types/boolean-operation)</summary>

### add()

```ts
add(): this
```

Additive boolean operation — fuses the result with all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### 'new'()

```ts
'new'(): this
```

No boolean operation — keeps the result as a standalone shape,
separate from all other scene objects.

### remove()

```ts
remove(): this
```

Subtractive boolean operation — cuts the result from all intersecting scene objects.
Use `.scope()` to target specific objects.

### scope()

```ts
scope(...objects: SceneObject[]): this
```

Narrows the boolean operation scope to specific target objects.
Must be chained after `.add()` or `.remove()`.

| `...objects` | [SceneObject](/docs/api/types/scene-object)[] | The target objects to operate on. *(optional)* |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inherited from [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)</summary>

### name()

```ts
name(value: string): this
```

Sets a custom display name for this object, overriding the default type-based name.

| `value` | string | The display name to assign. |

### reusable()

```ts
reusable(): this
```

Marks this object as reusable. Reusable objects retain their shapes when
consumed by features (e.g., extrude, revolve), allowing multiple features
to reference the same source geometry. Use `remove(obj)` to force-remove
shapes from a reusable object.

</details>

## Methods

### startFaces()

```ts
startFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the faces lying on the target surface (the base of the wrap).

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endFaces()

```ts
endFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the raised (or recessed) faces offset from the target surface by the wrap thickness.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### startEdges()

```ts
startEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the base faces of the wrap.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### endEdges()

```ts
endEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the offset faces of the wrap.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideFaces()

```ts
sideFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the wall faces created from the outer boundary of each wrapped region.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### sideEdges()

```ts
sideEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges on the wall faces, excluding edges shared with base/offset faces.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalFaces()

```ts
internalFaces(...args: (number | FaceFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects the wall faces created from holes inside a wrapped region.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| FaceFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or FaceFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### internalEdges()

```ts
internalEdges(...args: (number | EdgeFilterBuilder)[]): SceneObject
```

Selects edges bounding the hole walls of the wrap.

**Returns**: [`SceneObject`](/docs/api/types/scene-object)

| `...args` | (number \| EdgeFilterBuilder)[] | Numeric indices or EdgeFilterBuilder instances to filter the selection. *(optional)* |

### drill()

```ts
drill(value?: boolean): this
```

Enables or disables drill mode, which partitions the sketch into face regions
before wrapping.

| `value` | boolean | `true` to enable (default), `false` to disable. *(optional)* |


| `...points` | [Point2DLike](/docs/api/types/point2dlike)[] | 2D points in the sketch plane identifying regions to wrap. *(optional)* |

# Editor Setup

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/getting-started/editor-setup.mdx

sidebar_position: 2
title: "Editor Setup"

# Editor Setup

FluidCAD works with any text editor. It ships official extensions for VS Code and Neovim, and a CLI for everything else. All three options give you the same live 3D viewport — pick whichever fits your workflow.

## VS Code

1. Install the **FluidCAD** extension from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=FluidCAD.fluidcad).
2. Open your project folder in VS Code.
3. Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` on Windows/Linux, `Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS) and run **Show FluidCAD Scene**.

A 3D viewport opens in a side panel. It updates live as you edit any `.fluid.js` file.

## Neovim

Add the plugin with [lazy.nvim](https://github.com/folke/lazy.nvim):

```lua
{
  "Fluid-CAD/FluidCAD",
  config = function()
    require("fluidcad").setup()
  end,
  ft = { "javascript" },
}
```

Open a `.fluid.js` file — the server starts automatically. Run `:FluidCadOpenBrowser` to open the 3D viewport in your browser.

## Any other editor (CLI)

From your project directory, run:

```bash
npx fluidcad serve
```

This starts a local server at `http://localhost:3100`. Open that URL in your browser (or pass `--open` to launch it automatically) to see the 3D viewport. Edit your `.fluid.js` files in any editor — the viewport refreshes on save.

To run from elsewhere, point `-w` at your project: `npx fluidcad serve -w ./my-app`.

:::note
Interactive features like region picking, trimming, and interactive bezier drawing are only available with the VS Code and Neovim extensions. The CLI mode provides a view-only viewport that refreshes on save.
:::

| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `-w, --workspace <path>` | Path to your project | Current directory |
| `-p, --port <port>` | Server port | `3100` |
| `--open` | Open the viewport in your default browser when the server is ready | _off_ |

Run `npx fluidcad --help` to list every command, or `npx fluidcad serve --help` for the full flag reference.

---

# Installation

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/getting-started/installation.mdx

sidebar_position: 1
title: "Installation"

# Installation

FluidCAD is a JavaScript library for building parametric 3D models with code. You write `.fluid.js` files, and FluidCAD renders them in a live 3D viewport that updates as you type.

## Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) version 24 or higher
- npm (comes with Node.js)

## Create a new project

```bash
npm i fluidcad
npx fluidcad init
```

This creates a project with the following structure:

```
my-app/
├── package.json
├── jsconfig.json
├── init.js             ← required project entry point
└── test.fluid.js       ← your first model
```

:::note
FluidCAD files use the `.fluid.js` extension. The viewer only picks up files with this naming convention.
:::

:::note
FluidCAD is installed per-project and run with `npx fluidcad …`; a global install (`npm install -g fluidcad`) is not supported. The engine and your editor's type hints both resolve from the project's `node_modules`, so the package must live there. If you see `Cannot find module 'fluidcad' imported from …`, run `npm i fluidcad` inside the project.
:::

## The `init.js` file

Every FluidCAD project must have an `init.js` file at its root. This file initializes the FluidCAD engine and must be present before any `.fluid.js` files can run:

```js
import { init } from 'fluidcad';

export default await init();
```

Do not modify this file — it is generated automatically by `npx fluidcad init` and is required for the viewer to work.

## The starter file

Open `test.fluid.js` — this is the file that was generated for you:

```js
import { extrude, fillet, shell, sketch } from 'fluidcad/core';
import { circle } from 'fluidcad/core';

sketch("xy", () => {
    circle(50)
})

const e = extrude(50)

shell(-6, e.endFaces())

fillet(5, e.startEdges())
```

Here's what each line does:

1. **`sketch("xy", () => { ... })`** — Starts a 2D sketch on the XY plane (the horizontal plane). Everything inside the callback draws 2D shapes.
2. **`circle(50)`** — Draws a circle with a diameter of 50.
3. **`extrude(50)`** — Takes the sketch and pulls it up 50 units into a 3D solid. We store the result in `e` so we can reference its faces and edges later.
4. **`shell(-6, e.endFaces())`** — Hollows out the solid with a wall thickness of 6, removing the top face (`endFaces()`). The negative value means the shell goes inward.
5. **`fillet(5, e.startEdges())`** — Rounds the bottom edges with a radius of 5.

The result is a small cup-like shape. Next, let's set up your editor so you can see it in 3D.

---

# User Interface

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/getting-started/user-interface.mdx

sidebar_position: 4
title: "User Interface"

# User Interface

Once your editor is set up and your model is rendering, here's what you'll see in the FluidCAD viewport.

![FluidCAD User Interface](/img/docs/ui/FluidCAD%20-%20User%20Interface.png)

| # | Element | Description |
|---|---------|-------------|
| 1 | **File name** | The name of the currently open `.fluid.js` file. |
| 2 | **History panel** | Lists every feature (operation) in your model, in order. |
| 3 | **Feature status** | A checkmark means the feature was served from cache. A refresh icon means it was re-computed. |
| 4 | **Feature name** | Click a feature name to rollback the model to that point in the history. Double-click to insert a `breakpoint()` at that feature. |
| 5 | **Shapes panel** | Lists all solid shapes produced by the model. |
| 6 | **Shape property** | Gives information about the solid mesh, such as center of mass. |
| 7 | **Show/Hide grid** | Toggles the background grid on or off. |
| 8 | **Perspective camera** | Switches to perspective projection (objects farther away appear smaller). |
| 9 | **Orthographic camera** | Switches to orthographic projection (no perspective distortion). |
| 10 | **Fit model into view** | Resets the camera to fit the entire model in the viewport. |

## Breakpoints

A `breakpoint()` statement pauses model evaluation at that line, rolling the viewport back to that point so you can tweak the feature above it (or anything before it) and see the result in isolation. Remove the statement to resume full evaluation.

You can add one in several ways:

- **From the viewport** — double-click a feature name in the history panel to insert a `breakpoint()` right after that feature in the source file.
- **VS Code** — click the gutter next to any line in a `.fluid.js` file (just like setting a debugger breakpoint) and a `breakpoint()` statement is inserted at that line. You can also run **FluidCAD: Toggle Breakpoint** from the Command Palette.
- **Neovim** — run `:FluidCadToggleBreakpoint` to insert a `breakpoint()` at the current line.

---

# Your First Model

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/getting-started/your-first-model.mdx

sidebar_position: 3
title: "Your First Model"

import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';
import firstModelStep2 from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/first-model-step2.js';
import firstModelStep4 from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/first-model-step4.js';
import firstModelStep5 from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/first-model-step5.js';
import firstModelFinal from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/first-model-final.js';

# Your First Model

In this tutorial you'll build a small open-top container with rounded corners. Along the way you'll learn the core workflow: **sketch → extrude → modify**.

Create a new file called `box.fluid.js` in your project folder.

## Step 1: Import what you need

```js
import { sketch, extrude, shell, fillet } from 'fluidcad/core';
import { rect } from 'fluidcad/core';
```

Everything you need comes from `fluidcad/core`. Later guides will introduce `fluidcad/filters` for advanced selections.

## Step 2: Sketch a rectangle

```js
sketch("xy", () => {
    rect(100, 60)
})
```

`sketch("xy", ...)` opens a 2D drawing on the XY plane (the ground plane, looking down from above). Inside the callback, `rect(100, 60)` draws a rectangle that is 100 wide and 60 tall.

You should see a flat rectangle in your viewport.

## Step 3: Extrude it into a box

<CodeBlock language="js">{firstModelStep2}</CodeBlock>

![Extruded rectangle](/img/docs/getting-started/first-model-step2.png)

`extrude(30)` pulls the sketch 30 units upward into a solid box.

Notice that we didn't pass the sketch to `extrude()` — FluidCAD automatically picks up the last sketch. Most operations work this way: `extrude()` grabs the last sketch, `fillet()` targets the last selection, and touching shapes auto-fuse into one solid. You can always be explicit when you need to, but smart defaults keep simple cases simple.

We save the result in `box` so we can reference its faces and edges later.

## Step 4: Round the corners

Let's make it nicer by rounding the rectangle's corners. Update the sketch:

<CodeBlock language="js">{firstModelStep4}</CodeBlock>

- `.centered()` moves the rectangle so its center sits at the origin.
- `.radius(8)` rounds all four corners with a radius of 8.

![Rounded box](/img/docs/getting-started/first-model-step4.png)

## Step 5: Fillet the bottom edges

Let's round the bottom edges of the box:

```js
fillet(3, box.startEdges())
```

`box.startEdges()` selects the edges at the bottom (start) of the extrusion. `fillet(3)` rounds them with a radius of 3.

![Box with filleted edges](/img/docs/getting-started/first-model-step5.png)

## Step 6: Shell it into a container

Finally, let's hollow out the box to turn it into an open-top container:

```js
shell(-2, box.endFaces())
```

- `shell(-2, box.endFaces())` removes the top face and hollows out the solid, leaving walls that are 2 units thick.
- The negative thickness means the shell goes **inward** — the outer shape stays the same.
- `box.endFaces()` tells `shell()` which face to remove — this becomes the opening.

![Finished container](/img/docs/getting-started/first-model-final.png)

## Full code

Here's the complete model:

<CodeBlock language="js">{firstModelFinal}</CodeBlock>

## What you learned

- **`sketch(plane, callback)`** draws 2D shapes on a plane
- **`extrude(distance)`** turns a sketch into a 3D solid
- **`fillet(radius, edges)`** rounds edges
- **`shell(thickness, faces)`** hollows out a solid into a thin-walled container
- Operations like `extrude` return objects with methods like `.endFaces()` and `.startEdges()` that let you reference specific geometry
- Most operations have smart defaults — `extrude()` picks up the last sketch, and touching shapes auto-fuse into one solid

You're ready to explore the [Guides](../guides) for deeper coverage of each feature.

---

# Chamfer

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/guides/3d-operations/chamfer.mdx

sidebar_position: 8
title: "Chamfer"

import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';
import chamferBasic from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/chamfer-basic.js';
import chamferAsymmetric from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/chamfer-asymmetric.js';

# Chamfer

`chamfer()` bevels edges with a flat cut, creating angled transitions between faces.

<CodeBlock language="js">{chamferBasic}</CodeBlock>

![Basic chamfer](/img/docs/3d-operations/chamfer-basic.png)

## Asymmetric chamfer

Specify two distances for an uneven bevel:

<CodeBlock language="js">{chamferAsymmetric}</CodeBlock>

![Asymmetric chamfer](/img/docs/3d-operations/chamfer-asymmetric.png)

## Targeting edges

Works the same way as fillet — pass specific edges or use the last selection:

```js
// Direct
chamfer(2, e.sideEdges())

// With select
import { select } from 'fluidcad/core';
import { edge } from 'fluidcad/filters';

select(edge().onPlane("xy", 30))
chamfer(4)
```

You can also pass multiple edge selections to chamfer them all at once:

```js
chamfer(2, e.endEdges(), e.sideEdges())
```

---

# Color

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/guides/3d-operations/color.mdx

sidebar_position: 12
title: "Color"

import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';
import colorExample from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/color-example.js';
import colorSurvivesFillet from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/color-survives-fillet.js';
import colorBleeding from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/color-bleeding.js';
import colorFuseFirstInput from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/color-fuse-first-input.js';
import colorFuseFirstUncolored from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/color-fuse-first-uncolored.js';

# Color

`color()` applies a color to faces or entire solids:

<CodeBlock language="js">{colorExample}</CodeBlock>

![Colored faces](/img/docs/3d-operations/color-example.png)

`color()` accepts named CSS colors (`"red"`, `"steelblue"`, `"tomato"`) and hex values (`"#e74c3c"`, `"#2ecc71"`).

## Color with selection

```js
select(face().parallelTo("xy"))
color("#3498db")               // color all horizontal faces

select(face().cylinder())
color("silver")                // color cylindrical faces
```

## Color preservation

Colors are preserved across modifications. You can color a face and then keep modifying the shape — fillet, chamfer, fuse, cut, and other operations all carry colors forward to the resulting faces.

<CodeBlock language="js">{colorSurvivesFillet}</CodeBlock>

![Color preserved through fillet](/img/docs/3d-operations/color-survives-fillet.png)

In this example the orange color is applied to the top face *before* the fillet. After the fillet runs, the new top face is still orange, and so is the fillet's arc face — colors transfer onto modified faces and bleed onto adjacent new geometry.

When a colored face is split (for example by a cut that bisects it), every surviving piece keeps the color. When a colored face is fully removed, its color is dropped.

## Color bleeding

When new geometry is fused or merged into a colored shape, the new faces inherit the color from the surrounding colored faces:

<CodeBlock language="js">{colorBleeding}</CodeBlock>

![Color bleeding onto fused geometry](/img/docs/3d-operations/color-bleeding.png)

Bleeding only spreads onto faces that came from new geometry — faces that already existed on a shape and were intentionally left uncolored stay uncolored. The same rule applies to fillet arcs, chamfer surfaces, and cut section faces.

## Explicit `fuse()` color rule

When you call `fuse()` directly, the **first input is dominant**:

- If the first input has any colors, they propagate to the result (and bleed onto the other inputs).
- If the first input has no colors, the result stays uncolored even if other inputs are colored.

<CodeBlock language="js">{colorFuseFirstInput}</CodeBlock>

![fuse() first input dominates](/img/docs/3d-operations/color-fuse-first-input.png)

If the first input is uncolored, no color is propagated — coloring later inputs has no effect on the result:

<CodeBlock language="js">{colorFuseFirstUncolored}</CodeBlock>

![fuse() first input uncolored — result stays uncolored](/img/docs/3d-operations/color-fuse-first-uncolored.png)

This gives you a predictable way to choose which input's coloring wins when merging solids explicitly: put the input whose coloring you want to keep first.

---

# Cut

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/guides/3d-operations/cut.mdx

sidebar_position: 3
title: "Cut"

import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';
import cutBasic from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/cut-basic.js';
import cutThrough from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/cut-through.js';

# Cut

`cut()` removes material from existing solids. It is a shortcut for a subtractive extrude (`extrude().remove()`). Sketch a profile on a face, then cut into the solid.

<CodeBlock language="js">{cutBasic}</CodeBlock>

![Basic cut](/img/docs/3d-operations/cut-basic.png)

## Through-all cut

<CodeBlock language="js">{cutThrough}</CodeBlock>

![Through-all cut](/img/docs/3d-operations/cut-through.png)

When called with no distance, `cut()` removes material through the entire solid.

## Cut to face

Like `extrude()`, `cut()` accepts a face reference, `'first-face'`, or `'last-face'` instead of a fixed distance:

```js
cut(targetFace)        // cut until the target face
cut('first-face')      // cut to the nearest face
cut('last-face')       // cut to the farthest face
```

See [Extrude — Extrude to face](/docs/guides/3d-operations/extrude#extrude-to-face) for detailed examples. The same rules apply: only **planar and cylindrical faces** are supported at the moment.

## Draft angle

```js
cut(20).draft(-5)              // cut with a 5° inward draft
```

## Region picking

When a sketch has multiple regions, use `.pick()` to select which region to cut:

```js
sketch(box.endFaces(), () => {
    circle(60)
    circle(30)
})

cut(10).pick([20, 0])          // cut only the ring region near [20, 0]
```

:::tip[Interactive mode]
Call `.pick()` with no arguments to enter interactive mode. Click on regions in the viewport to select them.
:::

:::caution[Region picking can be fragile]
When you pick a region by coordinates (or by clicking in interactive mode), those coordinates are saved in your code. If the sketch dimensions change later, the pick point may fall outside the resized regions, breaking the model.

This makes `.pick()` great for **fast prototyping** or models with fixed dimensions. For parametric models where dimensions are likely to change, prefer structuring your sketches so each sketch contains only the regions you need — avoiding the need for `.pick()` altogether.
:::

## Accessing geometry

```js
const c = cut(15)

c.startEdges()         // edges at the top of the cut
c.endEdges()           // edges at the bottom of the cut
c.internalEdges()      // edges created inside the solid
c.internalFaces()      // faces inside the cut pocket
```

## Fusion scope

By default, cut removes material from all intersecting solids. Use `.scope()` to narrow it:

```js
cut().remove().scope(box)      // cut only from the box, leaving other solids untouched
```

---

# Extrude

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/guides/3d-operations/extrude.mdx

sidebar_position: 2
title: "Extrude"

import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';
import extrudeBasic from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-basic.js';
import extrudeSymmetric from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-symmetric.js';
import extrudeDraft from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-draft.js';
import extrudeRegionPick from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-region-pick.js';
import extrudeToFace from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-to-face.js';
import extrudeToFaceBlend from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-to-face-blend.js';
import extrudeToFirstFace from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-to-first-face.js';
import extrudeToFirstFaceCylindrical from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-to-first-face-cylindrical.js';
import extrudeThin from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-thin.js';
import extrudeThinDual from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-thin-dual.js';
import extrudeThinOpen from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-thin-open.js';
import extrudeThinOpenDual from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/extrude-thin-open-dual.js';

# Extrude

`extrude()` pulls a sketch upward (along the plane's normal) into a solid. It's the most common way to turn a 2D profile into 3D geometry.

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeBasic}</CodeBlock>

![Basic extrude](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-basic.png)

## No-argument extrude

```js
extrude()                      // uses a default distance of 25
```

When called with no arguments, `extrude()` uses a default distance and supports interactive mouse input in the viewport — drag to set the distance visually.

## Symmetric extrude

Extrude equally in both directions from the sketch plane:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeSymmetric}</CodeBlock>

![Symmetric extrude](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-symmetric.png)

## Draft angle

Add a taper to the extrusion:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeDraft}</CodeBlock>

![Extrude with draft angle](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-draft.png)

## Extrude to face

Instead of a fixed distance, you can extrude until the solid reaches a target face. Pass a face reference to `extrude()`:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeToFace}</CodeBlock>

![Extrude to face](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-to-face.png)

Use `select()` with a face filter to grab the target face. The extrusion stops when it meets that face.

### Blending with non-planar faces

When the target face is angled or curved (e.g. from a drafted extrude), the extrusion end blends to match the face shape:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeToFaceBlend}</CodeBlock>

![Extrude to face with blending](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-to-face-blend.png)

The red face is the target — the extrusion conforms to its angled surface.

## Extrude to first / last face

Instead of selecting a specific face, use `'first-face'` or `'last-face'` to automatically extrude to the nearest or farthest intersecting face along the extrusion direction:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeToFirstFace}</CodeBlock>

![Extrude to first face](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-to-first-face.png)

With cylindrical targets, the extrusion blends to the curved surface:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeToFirstFaceCylindrical}</CodeBlock>

![Extrude to first face — cylindrical](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-to-first-face-cylindrical.png)

:::note
Extrude to face, `'first-face'`, and `'last-face'` currently work with **planar and cylindrical faces** only.
:::

## Thin extrude

`.thin()` creates a thin-walled solid by offsetting the profile edges instead of extruding a filled face. The offset distance controls the wall thickness:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeThin}</CodeBlock>

![Thin extrude](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-thin.png)

Positive values offset outward, negative values offset inward:

```js
extrude(30).thin(5)    // 5 units outward
extrude(30).thin(-5)   // 5 units inward
```

### Two-direction offset

Pass two values to offset in both directions. The second offset automatically goes in the opposite direction of the first:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeThinDual}</CodeBlock>

![Thin extrude — dual offset](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-thin-dual.png)

### Open profiles

Thin extrude also works with open profiles (unclosed curves). The ends are capped with straight lines:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeThinOpen}</CodeBlock>

![Thin extrude — open profile](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-thin-open.png)

Two-direction offset works with open profiles as well — the original curve is not used, only the two offset curves:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeThinOpenDual}</CodeBlock>

![Thin extrude — open profile dual offset](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-thin-open-dual.png)

Thin extrude works with all extrude modes — `.symmetric()`, `.draft()`, `.remove()`, two distances, and face targets.

## Region picking

When a sketch has multiple overlapping shapes that create several regions, use `.pick()` to select which region to extrude:

<CodeBlock language="js">{extrudeRegionPick}</CodeBlock>

![Region picking — ring extrusion](/img/docs/3d-operations/extrude-region-pick.png)

:::tip[Interactive mode]
Call `.pick()` with no arguments to enter interactive mode. Click on regions in the viewport to select them.
:::

:::caution[Region picking can be fragile]
When you pick a region by coordinates (or by clicking in interactive mode), those coordinates are saved in your code. If the sketch dimensions change later, the pick point may fall outside the resized regions, breaking the model.

This makes `.pick()` great for **fast prototyping** or models with fixed dimensions. For parametric models where dimensions are likely to change, prefer structuring your sketches so each sketch contains only the regions you need — avoiding the need for `.pick()` altogether.
:::

## Accessing geometry

```js
const e = extrude(30)

e.endFaces()       // top face(s)
e.startFaces()     // bottom face(s)
e.sideFaces()      // side face(s)
e.endEdges()       // edges on the top
e.startEdges()     // edges on the bottom
e.sideEdges()      // edges on the sides
e.internalEdges()  // edges created inside (from fusion)
e.internalFaces()  // faces created inside (from fusion)
```

## Fusion scope

By default, extrude fuses with any touching solid. Control this with:

```js
extrude(30).new()              // create a separate solid, don't fuse
extrude(30).add()              // fuse with all touching solids (default)
```

---

# Fillet

Source: https://github.com/fluid-cad/fluidcad/blob/main/website/docs/guides/3d-operations/fillet.mdx

sidebar_position: 7
title: "Fillet"

import CodeBlock from '@theme/CodeBlock';
import filletBasic from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/fillet-basic.js';
import fillet2d from '!!raw-loader!./_examples/fillet-2d.js';

# Fillet

`fillet()` rounds edges with a given radius, creating smooth transitions between faces.

<CodeBlock language="js">{filletBasic}</CodeBlock>

![Filleted box edges](/img/docs/3d-operations/fillet-basic.png)

## Targeting edges

Pass specific edges as the second argument:

```js
fillet(5, e.endEdges())        // top edges of the extrude
fillet(3, e.sideEdges())       // side edges
fillet(2, c.internalEdges())   // internal edges from a cut
```

## Using the last selection

If you don't specify edges, `fillet()` targets the last `select()` result:

```js
import { select } from 'fluidcad/core';
import { edge } from 'fluidcad/filters';

select(edge().verticalTo("xy"))
fillet(5)                      // fillets the selected vertical edges
```

## 2D fillet

`fillet()` also works inside sketches to round corners between lines:

<CodeBlock language="js">{fillet2d}</CodeBlock>

![2D fillet on a pentagon](/img/docs/3d-operations/fillet-2d.png)
